settled_decisions.product_ac5: Coexist — admin force-login must NOT evict the driver's own clarity-scout-token. No change to ClarityScoutAuthController:64/:66; pinned by ClarityScoutForceLoginControllerTest:58 and re-asserted in S7.
settled_decisions.rejected_c2: Do NOT replace the admin_impersonator session gate with a signed URL, and do NOT persist admin_impersonator on the users table. The session check at ClarityScoutForceLoginController:16 is the only staff gate on a route carrying 'auth' middleware alone (routes/web.php:105), and it guards a token that hard-bypasses kit/permission/feature checks in two places (ClarityScoutMiddleware:25, routes/channels.php:30).
settled_decisions.revoke_all_on_exit_is_correct: All three revokeTracked() call sites (ImpersonateController:32, :83, :94) end the impersonation, so revoking EVERY tracked force token there is the intended semantics and is preserved. S1 makes tracking driver-scoped and bounded so revocation becomes targetable and stops carrying pruned/dead ids — it must NOT be used to spare other drivers' tabs on exit, which would leave gate-bypassing tokens alive to their 60-minute TTL.

defects_addressed.H1: S3 + S4 + S2 — exit-admin becomes logged, announced and non-GET; the resulting force-login rejection now names a reason instead of a bare 403.
defects_addressed.H2: S5 + S6 — the Scout PWA's credential moves from an origin-shared localStorage slot to a tab-scoped slot for force-login tabs.
defects_addressed.H3: S1 — driver-keyed, prune-aware force-token tracking with legacy flat-shape tolerance.

subtasks.title: Driver-scope force-token session tracking (H3)
subtasks.approach: Replace the flat clarity_scout_force_token_ids list with a driver-keyed map so tracking is bounded, prune-aware and targetable, while keeping revoke-all as the default so every existing exit path behaves exactly as today. Tolerate the pre-deploy flat shape so in-flight admin sessions still revoke correctly on the first post-deploy exit.
intended_diffs: SESSION_KEY now holds array<int|string, list<int>> keyed by driver id instead of list<int> (line 39 comment + shape).

mintFor(): replace Session::push(SESSION_KEY, id) at :49 with a read-modify-write of the driver's bucket; have prune() return the driver's surviving token ids and store exactly those, so ids deleted by KEEP_PER_DRIVER pruning never linger in the session.

revokeTracked(?User $driver = null): null (all three current call sites pass nothing) pulls and deletes every bucket then forgets the key — identical observable behaviour to today. With a driver, pull only that driver's bucket and leave the rest.

Add a private normalise(mixed $raw): array that maps a legacy flat list<int> onto a single unscoped bucket, so a session written before deploy still revokes instead of throwing or silently no-opping (data_impact.backward_compatibility_risk).

Leave TTL_MINUTES=60, KEEP_PER_DRIVER=3 and prune()'s per-driver query untouched. Do NOT clear the bucket on mint — that re-breaks the PR #410 duplicate-GET case pinned at ClarityScoutForceLoginControllerTest:87.
Update the class docblock to describe the driver-keyed shape and state that revoke-all is the intended exit semantics.
blast_radius: auth/session: changes which personal_access_tokens rows are deleted and when
session payload shape change with live pre-deploy sessions in flight
force token is a gate bypass (ClarityScoutMiddleware:25, routes/channels.php:30) — over-revoking locks staff out mid-demo, under-revoking leaves a bypass credential alive to its 60-minute TTL

subtasks.title: Surface and audit force-login rejections (AC4)
subtasks.approach: Give both intentional blocks an explicit, human-readable reason and an activity_log row written BEFORE the abort, so a rejection is visible to the admin in the freshly opened tab and reconstructable afterwards. Keep the existing success log untouched.
intended_diffs: Replace the bare abort_unless(session()->has('admin_impersonator'), 403) at :16 with a guarded branch that first writes activity('clarity-scout-force-login') with properties ['outcome' => 'denied', 'reason' => 'admin_impersonator_missing', 'kit_id' => ...], then aborts 403 with an explicit message naming the cause and the remedy (admin mode ended or the admin session expired — return to the admin panel and re-enter admin mode).
Do the same for the :20 no-assigned-user case: log ['outcome' => 'denied', 'reason' => 'kit_has_no_assigned_user'] then keep the 404 with its existing message.
There is no resources/views/errors/403.blade.php override in this repo, so Laravel's framework error view renders the abort message verbatim — no new view file is needed for AC4.

Leave the success activity('clarity-scout-force-login') block at :26-34 and the view payload at :36-53 byte-identical; ClarityScoutForceLoginControllerTest:216 and ScoutSetPasswordControllerTest:273 pin them.
subtasks.ui_impact: The new force-login tab now renders a 403/404 page that names the reason instead of a bare status page. No admin-panel UI change.
blast_radius: auth gate response path — the 403 must still be a hard deny; only its message and audit trail change
adds rows to activity_log on every denied attempt

subtasks.title: Make exitAdminMode() observable (H1, server half)
subtasks.approach: Mirror leave()'s pattern: write an activity('impersonation') row before revoking, then flash a Filament notification so the admin sees that admin mode ended and that Login to Scout is now disabled. Revocation semantics stay revoke-all.
intended_diffs: exitAdminMode(Request $request): build activity('impersonation'), performedOn($request->user()) when present, and log 'Admin mode exited by '.session()->get('impersonator.name') — ordered BEFORE revokeTracked() exactly as leave() does at :75-83.
Keep ScoutForceTokens::revokeTracked() with no argument (revoke-all) and session()->forget('admin_impersonator').

Send a Filament Notification (warning) titled 'Admin mode exited' whose body states that Scout force-login is no longer available until admin mode is re-entered, so redirect()->back() is no longer a silent no-visible-change transition.

Do NOT reorder revokeTracked() relative to session()->invalidate() in impersonate() (:32) or leave() (:83) — the current order is required and reordering would make revocation a silent no-op (reconcile_notes.disagreed_and_how_settled).
subtasks.ui_impact: A warning notification now appears in the admin panel after exiting admin mode; the amber ADMIN MODE banner disappears on the same render.
blast_radius: auth/session: the only method that strips admin_impersonator

subtasks.title: Harden exit-admin against GET reachability (H1, route half)
subtasks.approach: A destructive, session-mutating action must not sit behind a GET that a prefetch, a history replay or a stray click can fire. Convert the route to POST and the banner link to a CSRF-protected form submit. Scope is exit-admin only.
intended_diffs: routes/web.php:45 — Route::get('auth/impersonate/exit-admin', ...) becomes Route::post(...), name unchanged so route('impersonate.exit-admin') keeps resolving.

impersonate.blade.php:6-8 — replace the <a href> wrapper with <form method="POST" action="{{ route('impersonate.exit-admin') }}"> + @csrf and an x-filament::button type="submit" color="warning"; keep the label and layout identical inside the existing flex row.

Leave the 'Leave' link (route('impersonate.leave'), blade :9-11 and :17-19) as a GET — it is out of the H1 mechanism and its effect is self-evident (full logout + redirect to Backyard). Noted rather than silently widened.
No other caller of route('impersonate.exit-admin') exists in app code (rg: blade, ImpersonateControllerTest:153, okf/concepts/impersonation.md only).
subtasks.ui_impact: The Exit Admin Mode control renders as a form submit button on every admin page. Visually unchanged.
blast_radius: auth/session: the exit-admin route contract changes verb — any bookmark or stale tab issuing GET now 405s instead of silently revoking (intended)
the banner blade renders on every page of the admin panel

subtasks.title: Add a tab-scoped Scout credential accessor
subtasks.approach: One small module that owns where the Scout PWA's credential lives, so the four existing readers stop reaching into localStorage directly. Force-login tabs mark themselves tab-scoped (sessionStorage, which survives reload and is not shared with other tabs); normal driver login keeps using localStorage so the PWA still rehydrates on relaunch.
intended_diffs: New module exporting the key constants currently duplicated as string literals (scanner_token / scanner_user / scanner_kit / scanner_is_impersonating / scanner_trips_enabled / scanner_enabled_map_layers / scanner_teammate_overlay_enabled).
markTabScoped(): writes a scout_credential_scope='tab' marker into sessionStorage. Called once, first thing, by forceAuthenticate().

resolveStorage(): returns sessionStorage when the marker is present, otherwise localStorage. Resolved per call so it is correct both on the force-login boot and on a reload of that same tab. Deliberately a marker check, not a read-through fallback — a force-login tab must never silently adopt the driver's own localStorage token.
getCredential(key) / setCredential(key, value) / removeCredential(key) / clearCredentials() wrapping the resolved storage in try/catch, matching the existing defensive style of auth.js safeParse().
No imports from this module yet, so nothing changes behaviourally until S6 lands.
subtasks.test_filter: n/a (no unit-test runner for JS in this repo — package.json exposes vite + playwright only; verified in S9)

subtasks.title: Route every Scout credential read/write through the accessor (H2)
subtasks.approach: Swap the direct localStorage calls in all four known readers/writers for the accessor in one change, so REST, boot and analytics agree on which credential this tab owns. Echo already receives its token as an argument and stays per-tab with no edit.
intended_diffs: fetch.js:24 — authHeaders() reads getCredential(TOKEN) instead of localStorage.getItem('scanner_token'). handleUnauthorized()'s three removals at :74-76 become clearCredentials(). Admin/Bird's-Eye mode branch (:16-23) untouched.

auth.js — forceAuthenticate() calls markTabScoped() BEFORE any write, then its writes at :207-209 land in the tab-scoped slot; store hydration (:37-39), login() writes (:118-120), logout() removals (:143-146), fetchUser() writes (:189-190), the persist* flag helpers (:57-80) and parseEnabledMapLayers() (:12-20) all move to the accessor so a force-login tab's flags and cached identity stay with that tab.

main.js:17-20 — validate the injected payload before booting: if token, user or kit is missing/empty, record a signed-out reason and route to /scout/login instead of calling forceAuthenticate() on a malformed object. Folds in prep's downgraded defence-in-depth item at zero extra file cost; it is defensive only (Q14 shows no realistic null-token path).
main.js:22 — the non-force boot reads getCredential(TOKEN), so a plain /scout reload in a force-login tab rehydrates that tab's driver and a reload in the driver's own tab rehydrates the driver.
track.js:15 — the analytics gate reads getCredential(TOKEN) so it cannot diverge from authHeaders().

echo.js needs no edit: connectEcho(token) already takes the token as an argument (:15, :40), so passing the tab's own token keeps realtime and REST on the same driver and closes the split-brain described in Q15.
subtasks.ui_impact: A second force-login tab no longer repoints an already-open Scout tab at a different driver. The driver's own PWA still rehydrates across reloads and relaunches.
blast_radius: client auth identity for every Scout PWA request — a mistake signs drivers out or leaves a tab authenticating as the wrong driver
touches the driver's normal-login rehydrate path (main.js:22), not just the force-login path
credential storage location changes with live PWA installs in the field; a driver mid-shift must not be logged out by the deploy (normal login stays on localStorage, so it is not)

subtasks.title: Playwright e2e: per-tab credential isolation
subtasks.approach: H2 is a multi-tab defect and is untestable in PHPUnit. The repo already has a Playwright harness (playwright.config.ts, tests/e2e/*.spec.ts) and a local-only /__qa/login lever that sets admin_impersonator directly, so drive two force-login tabs in one browser context and assert their identities stay separate.
intended_diffs: Sign in via /__qa/login (routes/web.php:182-194, .test-host gated) to obtain admin_impersonator, then open /scout/force-login/{kitA} and /scout/force-login/{kitB} as two pages in the same context.
Assert page A's outbound Authorization header (via page.route or a request listener) still carries driver A's bearer after page B has booted, and that /api/scout/me in page A resolves to driver A.
Assert a reload of page A keeps driver A (tab-scoped credential survives reload).
Assert the driver's own normal-login tab still rehydrates from localStorage after a reload, so S6 has not broken the field PWA path.

gate.why_not_stop: The plan exceeds the file preference but the excess is already partitioned along a clean seam: the server lane (S1-S4, S7, S8) and the client lane (S5, S6, S9) share zero files, zero symbols and zero test runners, and each closes its defects on its own. No node was padded — the 10th file is reached only because H2 has four independent localStorage readers that prep explicitly requires changing together (caution at proposed_changes[3]). Phase 4 should land it as two PRs rather than trim a defect.

split_recommendation.pick: Land the server lane first: S1, S2, S3, S4 + S7, S8 — 5 production files (ScoutForceTokens, ClarityScoutForceLoginController, ImpersonateController, routes/web.php, impersonate.blade.php), verified by PHPUnit. Then the client lane: S5, S6 + S9 — 5 production files (scoutCredentials.js, fetch.js, auth.js, main.js, track.js), verified by Playwright.
split_recommendation.reason: 10 production files across 4 concerns and two runtimes exceeds the <=6 preference, and the two lanes are genuinely independent: the server lane closes H1, H3 and AC4; the client lane closes H2. Splitting keeps each auth/session review reviewable in one sitting and lets the server lane (which carries the session-shape deploy hazard) ship and be observed before the client credential relocation follows. Reviewing them together would put a session payload migration and a field-PWA credential move in the same diff.
